accepted.s: Who founded the Asaf Jahi state of Hyderabad in 1724?
accepted.x: Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan Siddiqi founded the Asaf Jahi state and became its first Nizam.
accepted.tq: Identify the founder directly and distinguish him from the early successors.
accepted.sec: Asaf Jahi founding - founder's names and titles, Shakar Kheda, rulers in sequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Aurangzeb conferred the title Chin Qilich Khan, Farrukh Siyar conferred Nizam-ul-Mulk, and Muhammad Shah conferred Asaf Jah in 1725.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure title-giver pair and eliminate the swapped authorities.
accepted.sec: Asaf Jahi founding - founder's names and titles, Shakar Kheda, rulers in sequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the establishment of the Asaf Jahi state:
1. Farrukh Siyar appointed Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan as Mughal Governor of the Deccan.
2. He defeated Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda.
3. The independent Asaf Jahi state was established in 1748.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The state was established in 1724, not 1748; 1748 was the year of the founder's death.
accepted.tq: Find the changed date in the statement set.
accepted.sec: Asaf Jahi founding - founder's names and titles, Shakar Kheda, rulers in sequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Battle of Shakar Kheda, which enabled the establishment of the virtually independent Hyderabad state, was fought in:
accepted.x: Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan defeated Mubariz Khan at Shakar Kheda in 1724, the founding year of the Asaf Jahi state.
accepted.tq: Use the close-date discrimination method for founding year, title year and death year.
accepted.sec: Asaf Jahi founding - founder's names and titles, Shakar Kheda, rulers in sequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the first Nizam is correct?
o: He accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
He kept the Marathas out of Hyderabad during his lifetime.
He was defeated at Shakar Kheda by Mubariz Khan.
accepted.x: The first Nizam kept the Marathas out during his lifetime. He died in 1748; the Subsidiary Alliance was accepted much later by Nizam Ali Khan.
accepted.tq: Separate the founder's achievements from those of the later Nizam Ali Khan.
accepted.sec: Asaf Jahi founding - founder's names and titles, Shakar Kheda, rulers in sequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following rulers of Hyderabad in chronological order of their accession:
A. Salabat Jung
B. Nasir Jung
C. Muzaffar Jung
D. Asaf Jah I
E. Nizam Ali Khan
Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: The order is Asaf Jah I (1724), Nasir Jung (1748), Muzaffar Jung (1750), Salabat Jung (1751), and Nizam Ali Khan (1762).
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last rulers, then arrange the closely spaced middle accessions.
accepted.sec: Asaf Jahi founding - founder's names and titles, Shakar Kheda, rulers in sequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Nizam Ali Khan ruled from 1762 to 1803. The period 1751–1762 belonged to Salabat Jung.
accepted.tq: Check the ruler-period pair for a shifted succession date.
accepted.sec: Asaf Jahi founding - founder's names and titles, Shakar Kheda, rulers in sequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Ruler)
a. Sikandar Jah
b. Nasir-ud-Daula
c. Afzal-ud-Daula
d. Mir Mahbub Ali Khan

List-II (Period of rule)
i. 1857–1869
ii. 1803–1829
iii. 1869–1911
iv. 1829–1857

Select the correct answer.
accepted.x: Sikandar Jah ruled from 1803–1829, Nasir-ud-Daula from 1829–1857, Afzal-ud-Daula from 1857–1869, and Mir Mahbub Ali Khan from 1869–1911.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive period of Mir Mahbub Ali Khan and complete the sequence.
accepted.sec: Asaf Jahi founding - founder's names and titles, Shakar Kheda, rulers in sequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Asaf Jahi dynasty is correct?
o: Hyderabad State was integrated into the Indian Union through Operation Polo in 1948.
Mir Osman Ali Khan ruled from 1869 to 1911.
The dynasty continued as the ruling power after 1948.
Nizam Ali Khan was the last Nizam of Hyderabad.
accepted.x: Operation Polo integrated Hyderabad State into the Indian Union in 1948. Mir Osman Ali Khan was the last Nizam.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the end of the dynasty from the end of individual rulers.
accepted.sec: Asaf Jahi founding - founder's names and titles, Shakar Kheda, rulers in sequence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who wrote both History of Aurangzeb and Fall of the Mughal Empire?
accepted.x: Jadunath Sarkar authored both History of Aurangzeb and Fall of the Mughal Empire.
accepted.tq: Match the historian with the distinctive pair of works.
accepted.sec: Historiography of decline → historian and book  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The agrarian-crisis interpretation of Mughal decline, emphasising the over-exploitation of peasants and the resulting revolts, is associated with:
accepted.x: Irfan Habib explained the decline through an agrarian crisis in The Agrarian System of Mughal India (1963), arguing that over-exploitation of peasants provoked revolts.
accepted.tq: Link the interpretation to the historian rather than merely recalling the book title.
accepted.sec: Historiography of decline → historian and book  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which work is associated with Satish Chandra's explanation of the Mughal decline?
o: Parties and Politics at the Mughal Court, 1707–1740
accepted.x: Satish Chandra wrote Parties and Politics at the Mughal Court, 1707–1740 and associated decline with the jagirdari crisis.
accepted.tq: Use author–work discrimination among closely related historiographical titles.
accepted.sec: Historiography of decline → historian and book  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. M. Athar Ali — The Mughal Nobility under Aurangzeb
2. W. H. Moreland — India at the Death of Akbar
3. François Bernier — Travels in the Mogul Empire
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Athar Ali examined the Mughal nobility, Moreland wrote India at the Death of Akbar, and Bernier wrote Travels in the Mogul Empire.
accepted.tq: Verify each author–work pair before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Historiography of decline → historian and book  [APPSC]

accepted.s: M. Athar Ali attributed the worsening of the jagir shortage primarily to:
o: The transfer of all jagirs to European companies
The enlargement of the nobility through the inclusion of Deccanis and Marathas
The abolition of the mansabdari system by Farrukh Siyar
The decline of agriculture caused by Nadir Shah's raid
accepted.x: Athar Ali argued that the enlarged nobility, including Deccanis and Marathas, intensified the shortage of jagirs.
accepted.tq: Apply the historian's specific causal argument rather than choosing a general cause of decline.
accepted.sec: Historiography of decline → historian and book  [APPSC]

accepted.s: François Bernier's explanation of Mughal decline emphasised that:
o: The empire collapsed mainly because of the Maratha naval power.
The jagirdari crisis resulted from too few nobles in the imperial service.
The absence of private property in land reduced the incentive for improvement and led towards ruin.
Aurangzeb's religious policy alone caused the complete collapse of agriculture.
accepted.x: Bernier associated the absence of private property in land with a lack of incentive to improve it and predicted ruin.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise argument attached to the named historian.
accepted.sec: Historiography of decline → historian and book  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The revisionist interpretation of the eighteenth century views it chiefly as a period of:
o: Exclusive European control over the peasant surplus
Regional growth, with successor states controlling economic and law-and-order systems
Uninterrupted Mughal centralisation under weak successors
accepted.x: The revisionist view treats the eighteenth century as a period of regional growth. The new states managed their own economic and law-and-order systems and controlled peasant surplus.
accepted.tq: Contrast the revisionist regional-growth interpretation with the older collapse narrative.
accepted.sec: Historiography of decline → historian and book  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a major cause of the decline of the Mughal Empire?
o: The invasions of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali
The long Deccan wars and the resulting drain on the treasury
The strengthening of central authority by independent nobles
accepted.x: Independent nobles weakened, rather than strengthened, central authority. The Deccan wars, Maratha rise and invasions were among the major causes of decline.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed effect in a cause-of-decline option.
accepted.sec: Causes of decline

accepted.s: At its greatest extent under Aurangzeb, the Mughal Empire extended approximately from:
o: Kashmir to Jinji and the Hindukush to Chittagong
Kabul to Bijapur and Sindh to Assam
Punjab to Madurai and the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal
Delhi to the Narmada and Gujarat to Bengal
accepted.x: Under Aurangzeb the empire reached from Kashmir to Jinji and from the Hindukush to Chittagong.
accepted.tq: Recall both geographical limits together instead of relying on one directional clue.
accepted.sec: Causes of decline

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of Mughal decline:
1. Aurangzeb's long Deccan wars weakened the foundations of the empire and drained the treasury.
2. The Sayyids' control contributed to corruption and mismanagement.
3. Peasant and zamindar revolts followed the jagirdari and agrarian crises.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Religious policies, prolonged warfare, factional noble politics, fiscal crisis and agrarian unrest combined to weaken the empire.
accepted.tq: Test cumulative causation by checking each internal cause separately.
accepted.sec: Causes of decline

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with a cause of Mughal decline?
o: European companies — a factor contributing to the decline
Noble rivalries — weakening of central authority
Maratha rise — restoration of Mughal authority
Agrarian crisis — shrinkage of the fiscal base
accepted.x: The Maratha rise weakened Mughal authority; it did not restore it. Noble rivalries, agrarian crisis and European companies were associated with the decline.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed consequence in a cause-and-effect pair.
accepted.sec: Causes of decline

accepted.s: The Farman of 1717 issued by Farrukh Siyar is significant because it:
o: Granted chauth and sardeshmukhi to Shahu's agent
Exempted the English Company from customs duties in Bengal
Granted the Company Diwani rights in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
Transferred Kora and Allahabad to the Company
accepted.x: The Farman of 1717 exempted the Company from customs duties in Bengal and was called the Company's Magna Carta.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the 1717 Farman from the 1765 Treaty of Allahabad.
accepted.sec: Treaties and titles granted by later Mughals

accepted.s: The Mughal grant of 1719, issued through the Sayyids, granted to Balaji Vishwanath, as Shahu's agent:
o: Diwani rights in Bengal and Bihar
Kora and Allahabad with an annual payment
Chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas
accepted.x: The 1719 grant recognised Shahu's claim to chauth and sardeshmukhi from the six Deccan subas through his agent Balaji Vishwanath.
accepted.tq: Separate the content of the 1719 grant from the later Company concessions.
accepted.sec: Treaties and titles granted by later Mughals

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Treaty of Allahabad of 1765?
o: The Sayyids granted the Company chauth of the Deccan subas.
Shah Alam II granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
Farrukh Siyar exempted the Company from customs duties in Bengal.
Akbar II granted the Company the title of Raja.
accepted.x: Under the Treaty of Allahabad, Shah Alam II granted the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. The emperor received Kora and Allahabad and an annual payment of Rs 26 lakh.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct grantor and the precise territorial content of the treaty.
accepted.sec: Treaties and titles granted by later Mughals

accepted.s:
With reference to the Treaty of Allahabad, consider the following statements:
1. Shah Alam II received Kora and Allahabad.
2. The emperor was entitled to an annual payment of Rs 26 lakh.
3. Warren Hastings continued this annual payment without interruption after 1772.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. From 1772 Warren Hastings stopped the annual grant and sold Kora and Allahabad to the Nawab of Awadh.
accepted.tq: Use the date-based exception to identify the false continuation claim.
accepted.sec: Treaties and titles granted by later Mughals

accepted.s: The decline of the Mughal Empire created a power vacuum that was successively filled by:
o: Regional states, the Marathas and finally the East India Company
The Rajputs, the Sikhs and the Portuguese
The Mughals, the Marathas and the Ottoman Empire
The Sayyids, the Afghans and the French alone
accepted.x: The decline opened space for regional successor states, the Marathas and ultimately the East India Company.
accepted.tq: Recall the broad political sequence following imperial decline.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Diwani granted in 1765 is regarded as the East India Company's:
o: First exemption from customs duties in Bengal
accepted.x: The Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, obtained in 1765, provided the Company's legal foothold for territorial and fiscal power in India.
accepted.tq: Link the constitutional-financial concession with its wider historical significance.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Golconda became the 21st Mughal suba after its fall in 1687.
2. The Asaf Jahi state of Hyderabad grew out of the Mughal Deccan.
3. The Nizam accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Golconda was incorporated as the 21st Mughal suba in 1687, Hyderabad emerged from the Mughal Deccan, and the Nizam accepted the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798.
accepted.tq: Combine the Andhra-specific administrative, regional and treaty facts in one coded set.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Who was the first Mughal pensioner of the East India Company?
accepted.x: Shah Alam II became the first Mughal pensioner of the East India Company.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first pensioner from the last emperor and the later titular ruler.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the last rulers in the stated categories?
o: Bahadur Shah Zafar — last Mughal emperor; Asaf Jah I — last Nizam
Bahadur Shah Zafar — last Mughal emperor; Mir Osman Ali Khan — last Nizam
Akbar II — last Mughal emperor; Mir Mahbub Ali Khan — last Nizam
Shah Alam II — last Mughal emperor; Nizam Ali Khan — last Nizam
accepted.x: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal emperor, while Mir Osman Ali Khan was the last Nizam of Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Compare parallel 'last' designations and avoid substituting an earlier ruler.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the raids of Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali?
o: Nadir Shah took Punjab, whereas Abdali took the Koh-i-Noor and Peacock Throne.
Nadir Shah's raid occurred in 1739, while Abdali's raids began from 1748.
Nadir Shah's raids began in 1748, while Abdali invaded in 1739.
Both raids began in 1761 and ended with the Battle of Panipat.
accepted.x: Nadir Shah raided India in 1739, taking the Koh-i-Noor and Peacock Throne. Abdali's raids began from 1748, took Punjab and culminated in Panipat in 1761.
accepted.tq: Separate the two invaders by starting date and the distinctive result of each raid.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Nadir Shah's raid of 1739 resulted in the removal of which of the following from India?
o: The Koh-i-Noor and the Peacock Throne
The Diwani and the Farman of 1717
accepted.x: Nadir Shah carried away the Koh-i-Noor and the Peacock Throne during his raid of 1739.
accepted.tq: Match the invader with the distinctive objects taken during the raid.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 is associated with the raids of:
accepted.x: Ahmad Shah Abdali's raids, which began from 1748, culminated in the Battle of Panipat in 1761.
accepted.tq: Identify the invader from the terminal event in the sequence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
